large\nbiological sequences or sets of sequences.
#> 342                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         systemPipeR is a workflow management environment for\nreproducible data analysis that integrates R with command-line\nsoftware. It enables researchers to design, execute, and report\ncomplex workflows on local machines and HPC systems. The\nframework combines R-based analysis with external tools through\na Common Workflow Language (CWL) interface, manages workflow\ndependencies and restart capabilities, and automatically\ngenerates reproducible scientific analysis reports. The\ncompanion package systemPipeRdata provides ready-to-use\nworkflow templates that simplify workflow setup and\ncustomization. Alternatively, workflow templates can be loaded\nfrom dedicated GitHub repositories.

                                                                                                        To classify Helicobacter pylori genomes according to\ngenetic distance from nine reference populations. The nine\nreference populations are hpgpAfrica, hpgpAfrica-distant,\nhpgpAfroamerica, hpgpEuroamerica, hpgpMediterranea, hpgpEurope,\nhpgpEurasia, hpgpAsia, and hpgpAklavik86-like. The vertex\npopulations are Africa, Europe and Asia.
#> 344                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    This package implements functions to analyze multi-omics\nepigenetic data. Data of fragment type and base type are\nsupported by epiSeeker. It provides functions to retrieve the\nnearest genes around the peak, annotate genomic region of the\npeak, statistical methods to estimate the significance of\noverlap among peak data sets, and motif analysis. It\nincorporates the GEO database for users to compare their own\ndataset with those deposited in the database. The comparison\ncan be used to infer cooperative regulation and thus can be\nused to generate hypotheses. Several visualization functions\nare implemented to summarize the coverage of the peak\nexperiment, average profile and heatmap of peaks binding to TSS\nregions, genomic annotation, distance to TSS, overlap of peaks\nor genes, and the single-base resolution epigenetic data by\nconsidering the strand, motif, and additional information.

                                                                                      cogeqc aims to facilitate systematic quality checks on\nstandard comparative genomics analyses to help researchers\ndetect issues and select the most suitable parameters for each\ndata set. cogeqc can be used to asses: i. genome assembly and\nannotation quality with BUSCOs and comparisons of statistics\nwith publicly available genomes on the NCBI; ii. orthogroup\ninference using a protein domain-based approach and; iii.\nsynteny detection using synteny network properties. There are\nalso data visualization functions to explore QC summary\nstatistics.

The package is\nparticularly useful for bioinformatics applications but can be\nused for any multi-set analysis.

                                                                                                                                                         BatchSVG is a method to identify batch-biased spatially\nvariable genes (SVGs) in spatial transcriptomics data. The\nbatch variable can be defined as sample, donor sex, or other\nbatch effects of interest. The BatchSVG method is based on the\nbinomial deviance model (Townes et al, 2019).

                    GOfan provides an intuitive and compact visualization of\nGene Ontology (GO) enrichment results using a sunburst layout\ninspired by SynGO, preserving hierarchical relationships among\nGO terms and allowing color-based encoding of information such\nas p-values or gene counts. By converting complex GO DAGs into\nclean, circular representations, it allows researchers to\nquickly grasp the hierarchical structure and biological\nsignificance of enriched terms. The interactive and\ncustomizable visualizations facilitate exploration of key GO\ncategories, enhancing interpretation and presentation of\nenrichment analyses.
#> 351                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         The damidBind package provides a straightforward formal\nanalysis pipeline to analyse and explore differential DamID\nbinding, gene transcription or chromatin accessibility between\ntwo conditions. The package imports processed data from\nDamID-seq experiments, either as external raw files in the form\nof binding bedGraphs and GFF/BED peak calls, or as internal\nlists of GRanges objects. After optionally normalising data,\ncombining peaks across replicates and determining per-replicate\npeak occupancy, the package links bound loci to nearby genes.\nFor RNA Polymerase DamID data, the package calculates occupancy\nover genes, and optionally calcualates the FDR of\nsignificantly-enriched gene occupancy. damidBind then uses\neither limma (for conventional log2 ratio DamID binding data)\nor NOIseq (for counts-based CATaDa chromatin accessibility\ndata) to identify differentially-enriched regions, or\ndifferentially epxressed genes, between two conditions. The\npackage provides a number of visualisation tools (volcano\nplots, Gene Ontology enrichment plots via ClusterProfiler and\nproportional Venn diagrams via BioVenn for downstream data\nexploration and analysis. An powerful, interactive IGV genome\nbrowser interface (powered by Shiny and igvShiny) allows users\nto rapidly and intuitively assess significant\ndifferentially-bound regions in their genomic context.
#> 352                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         The GENESIS package provides methodology for estimating,\ninferring, and accounting for population and pedigree structure\nin genetic analyses.  The current implementation provides\nfunctions to perform PC-AiR (Conomos et al., 2015, Gen Epi) and\nPC-Relate (Conomos et al., 2016, AJHG). PC-AiR performs a\nPrincipal Components Analysis on genome-wide SNP data for the\ndetection of population structure in a sample that may contain\nknown or cryptic relatedness. Unlike standard PCA, PC-AiR\naccounts for relatedness in the sample to provide accurate\nancestry inference that is not confounded by family structure.\nPC-Relate uses ancestry representative principal components to\nadjust for population structure/ancestry and accurately\nestimate measures of recent genetic relatedness such as kinship\ncoefficients, IBD sharing probabilities, and inbreeding\ncoefficients. Additionally, functions are provided to perform\nefficient variance component estimation and mixed model\nassociation testing for both quantitative and binary\nphenotypes.

                        Our scLANE model uses truncated power basis spline models\nto build flexible, interpretable models of single cell gene\nexpression over pseudotime or latent time. Battlefield is a Swiss-army toolkit originally developed\nto define and extract spatial spots from specific tissue\nregions—such as front regions, niche borders, invasive margins,\nand cluster interfaces—using spatial transcriptomics data or\nclustered tissue maps. It has since been extended to support\ntrajectory selection and layer inspection, and now provides a\ncollection of low-level utilities for spatial transcriptomics\nanalysis. These utilities are primarily intended to be reused\nwithin higher-level analytical packages. It is designed to work\nwith sequencing-based platforms such as Visium at several\nresolutions and Visium HD(binned).

#> 366                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Extends the Seurat classes and functions to support\nGenomic Data Structure (GDS) files as a DelayedArray backend\nfor data representation. It relies on the implementation of\nGDS-based DelayedMatrix in the SCArray package to represent\nsingle cell RNA-seq data. The common optimized algorithms\nleveraging GDS-based and single cell-specific DelayedMatrix\n(SC_GDSMatrix) are implemented in the SCArray package.\nSCArray.sat introduces a new SCArrayAssay class (derived from\nthe Seurat Assay), which wraps raw counts, normalized\nexpressions and scaled data matrix based on GDS-specific\nDelayedMatrix. It is designed to integrate seamlessly with the\nSeurat package to provide common data analysis in the\nSeuratObject-based workflow. Compared with Seurat, SCArray.sat\nsignificantly reduces the memory usage without downsampling and\ncan be applied to very large datasets.

                                                  IONiseR provides tools for the quality assessment of\nOxford Nanopore MinION data.                                                           Provides means to interactively visualize guide RNAs\n(gRNAs) in GuideSet objects via Shiny application.                           MSstats package provide tools for preprocessing,\nsummarization and differential analysis of mass spectrometry\n(MS) proteomics data. The\npackage can provide data in either tabular format or with\nMultiAssayExperiment object that uses familiar Bioconductor\ndata representations.

                                  MeLSI (Metric Learning for Statistical Inference) is a\nnovel machine learning method for microbiome data analysis that\nlearns optimal distance metrics to improve statistical power in\ndetecting group differences. Unlike traditional distance\nmetrics (Bray-Curtis, Euclidean, Jaccard), MeLSI adapts to the\nspecific characteristics of your dataset to maximize separation\nbetween groups. The method uses an ensemble of weak learners to\nidentify which microbial features drive group differences,\nproviding both improved statistical power and biological\ninterpretability through feature importance weights.
#> 372                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        SingleMoleculeFootprinting provides functions to analyze\nSingle Molecule Footprinting (SMF) data. Following the workflow\nexemplified in its vignette, the user will be able to perform\nbasic data analysis of SMF data with minimal coding effort.\nStarting from an aligned bam file, we show how to perform\nquality controls over sequencing libraries, extract methylation\ninformation at the single molecule level accounting for the two\npossible kind of SMF experiments (single enzyme or double\nenzyme), classify single molecules based on their patterns of\nmolecular occupancy, plot SMF information at a given genomic\nlocation.

        SpaceTrooper performs Quality Control analysis using data\ndriven GLM models of Image-Based spatial data, providing\nexploration plots, QC metrics computation, outlier detection.\nIt implements a GLM strategy for the detection of low quality\ncells in imaging-based spatial data (Transcriptomics and\nProteomics). It additionally implements several plots for the\nvisualization of imaging based polygons through the ggplot2\npackage.
#> 376                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         In high resolution mass spectrometry (HR-MS), the measured\nmasses can be decomposed into potential element combinations\n(chemical sum formulas). Where additional mass/intensity\ninformation of respective isotopic peaks is available,\ndecomposition can take this information into account to better\nrank the potential candidate sum formulas. To compare measured\nmass/intensity information with the theoretical distribution of\ncandidate sum formulas, the latter needs to be calculated. This\npackage implements fast algorithms to address both tasks, the\ncalculation of isotopic distributions for arbitrary sum\nformulas (assuming a HR-MS resolution of roughly 30,000), and\nthe ranked list of sum formulas fitting an observed peak or\nisotopic peak set.

package with a stand-alone Java\napplication for interactive visualization and manipulation of\nnested networks. Graph, node, and edge attributes can be\nconfigured using either graphical or command-line methods,\nfollowing igraph syntax rules.
#> 380                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     An extensive set of data (pre-)processing and analysis\nmethods and tools for metabolomics and other omics, with a\nstrong emphasis on statistics and machine learning. This\ntoolbox allows the user to build extensive and standardised\nworkflows for data analysis. The methods and tools have been\nimplemented using class-based templates provided by the struct\n(Statistics in R Using Class-based Templates) package. The\ntoolbox includes pre-processing methods (e.g. signal drift and\nbatch correction, normalisation, missing value imputation and\nscaling), univariate (e.g. ttest, various forms of ANOVA,\nKruskal–Wallis test and more) and multivariate statistical\nmethods (e.g. PCA and PLS, including cross-validation and\npermutation testing) as well as machine learning methods (e.g.\nSupport Vector Machines). Ontology terms have been integrated\nto provide standardised definitions for the different methods,\ninputs and outputs.

                                                  MIRit is an R package that provides several methods for\ninvestigating the relationships between miRNAs and genes in\ndifferent biological conditions. In particular, MIRit allows to\nexplore the functions of dysregulated miRNAs, and makes it\npossible to identify miRNA-gene regulatory axes that control\nbiological pathways, thus enabling the users to unveil the\ncomplexity of miRNA biology. MIRit is an all-in-one framework\nthat aims to help researchers in all the central aspects of an\nintegrative miRNA-mRNA analyses, from differential expression\nanalysis to network characterization.

                                                                                         BreastSubtypeR provides an assumption-aware, multi-method\nframework for intrinsic molecular subtyping of breast cancer.\nThe package harmonizes several published nearest-centroid (NC)\nand single-sample predictor (SSP) classifiers, supplies\nmethod-specific preprocessing and robust probe-to-gene mapping,\nand implements a cohort-aware AUTO mode that selectively\nenables classifiers compatible with the cohort composition. A\nlocal Shiny app (iBreastSubtypeR) is included for interactive\nanalyses and to support users without programming experience.

                                                            This package estimates tumor purity, copy number, and loss\nof heterozygosity (LOH), and classifies single nucleotide\nvariants (SNVs) by somatic status and clonality. PureCN is\ndesigned for targeted short read sequencing data, integrates\nwell with standard somatic variant detection and copy number\npipelines, and has support for tumor samples without matching\nnormal samples.
#> 387                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Fit a latent embedding multivariate regression (LEMUR)\nmodel to multi-condition single-cell data. The model provides a\nparametric description of single-cell data measured with\ntreatment vs. control or more complex experimental designs. The\nparametric model is used to (1) align conditions, (2) predict\nlog fold changes between conditions for all cells, and (3)\nidentify cell neighborhoods with consistent log fold changes.\nFor those neighborhoods, a pseudobulked differential expression\ntest is conducted to assess which genes are significantly\nchanged.

                                                                                                    svaRetro contains functions for detecting retrotransposed\ntranscripts (RTs) from structural variant calls. It takes\nstructural variant calls in GRanges of breakend notation and\nidentifies RTs by exon-exon junctions and insertion sites. The\ncandidate RTs are reported by events and annotated with\ninformation of the inserted transcripts.

                                                                                                                                                                  Implements a variety of methods for combining p-values in\ndifferential analyses of genome-scale datasets. Functions can\ncombine p-values across different tests in the same analysis\n(e.g., genomic windows in ChIP-seq, exons in RNA-seq) or for\ncorresponding tests across separate analyses (e.g., replicated\ncomparisons, effect of different treatment conditions). Support\nis provided for handling log-transformed input p-values,\nmissing values and weighting where appropriate.
#> 390                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  RTNsurvival integrates regulons inferred by the RTN\npackage with survival data. For each regulon, a two-tailed GSEA\nframework computes a differential Enrichment Score (dES) at the\nindividual-sample level. The resulting dES distribution across\nsamples is then used to evaluate survival associations within\nthe cohort. Two primary workflows are supported: (i) Cox\nproportional hazards models, in which regulon activities are\ntreated as predictors of survival time, and (ii) Kaplan–Meier\nanalyses assessing cohort stratification based on regulon\nactivity. All graphical outputs are customizable according to\nuser specifications.

co-regulatory loops between pairs of\nregulons inferred by the RTN package by evaluating their shared\ntarget genes. It infers dual regulons and tests whether\nregulator pairs exhibit cooperative or competitive influences\non common targets.
#> 392                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           A transcriptional regulatory network (TRN) consists of a\ncollection of transcription factors (TFs) and the regulated\ntarget genes. TFs are regulators that recognize specific DNA\nsequences and guide the expression of the genome, either\nactivating or repressing the expression the target genes. The\nset of genes controlled by the same TF forms a regulon. This\npackage provides classes and methods for the reconstruction of\nTRNs and analysis of regulons.

                                                             Provides visualization functionality for untargeted LC-MS\nmetabolomics research. Includes quality control visualizations,\nfeature-wise visualizations and results visualizations.
#> 394                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Mutational processes leave characteristic footprints in\ngenomic DNA. This package provides a comprehensive set of\nflexible functions that allows researchers to easily evaluate\nand visualize a multitude of mutational patterns in base\nsubstitution catalogues of e.g. healthy samples, tumour\nsamples, or DNA-repair deficient cells. The package covers a\nwide range of patterns including: mutational signatures,\ntranscriptional and replicative strand bias, lesion\nsegregation, genomic distribution and association with genomic\nfeatures, which are collectively meaningful for studying the\nactivity of mutational processes. The package works with single\nnucleotide variants (SNVs), insertions and deletions (Indels),\ndouble base substitutions (DBSs) and larger multi base\nsubstitutions (MBSs). The package provides functionalities for\nboth extracting mutational signatures de novo and determining\nthe contribution of previously identified mutational signatures\non a single sample level. MutationalPatterns integrates with\ncommon R genomic analysis workflows and allows easy association\nwith (publicly available) annotation data.
#> 395                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   CARD is a reference-based deconvolution method that\nestimates cell type composition in spatial transcriptomics\nbased on cell type specific expression information obtained\nfrom a reference scRNA-seq data. A key feature of CARD is its\nability to accommodate spatial correlation in the cell type\ncomposition across tissue locations, enabling accurate and\nspatially informed cell type deconvolution as well as refined\nspatial map construction. CARD relies on an efficient\noptimization algorithm for constrained maximum likelihood\nestimation and is scalable to spatial transcriptomics with tens\nof thousands of spatial locations and tens of thousands of\ngenes.

                                                                                                                                                cfDNA fragments carry important features for building\ncancer sample classification ML models, such as fragment size,\nand fragment end motif etc. Analyzing and visualizing fragment\nsize metrics, as well as other biological features in a\ncurated, standardized, scalable, well-documented, and\nreproducible way might be time intensive. This package intends\nto resolve these problems and simplify the process. It offers\ntwo sets of functions for cfDNA feature characterization and\nvisualization.
#> 398                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            sRACIPE implements a randomization-based method for gene\ncircuit modeling. It allows us to study the effect of both the\ngene expression noise and the parametric variation on any gene\nregulatory circuit (GRC) using only its topology, and simulates\nan ensemble of models with random kinetic parameters at\nmultiple noise levels. Statistical analysis of the generated\ngene expressions reveals the basin of attraction and stability\nof various phenotypic states and their changes associated with\nintrinsic and extrinsic noises. sRACIPE provides a holistic\npicture to evaluate the effects of both the stochastic nature\nof cellular processes and the parametric variation.

                                                      BLASE is a method for finding where bulk RNA-seq data lies\non a single-cell pseudotime trajectory. It uses a fast and\nunderstandable approach based on Spearman correlation, with\nbootstrapping to provide confidence. BLASE can be used to\n"date" bulk RNA-seq data, annotate cell types in scRNA-seq, and\nhelp correct for developmental phenotype differences in bulk\nRNA-seq experiments.

High-throughput extensible toolkit for processing FASTQ\ndata. The goal of this package is to empower users to quickly\nbuild out small programmatic 'kernels' to define any FASTQ\nprocessing task they may need. Builds on Intel TBB’s flow graph\nto orchestrate concurrent I/O and data processing; throughput\ncan be as fast as compression and disk speed allows. The\npackage also ships with a suite of predefined kernels for\ncommon FASTQ tasks.

                                          Implements exact and approximate methods for nearest\nneighbor detection, in a framework that allows them to be\neasily switched within Bioconductor packages or workflows.\nExact searches can be performed using the k-means for k-nearest\nneighbors algorithm, vantage point trees, or an exhaustive\nsearch. Approximate searches can be performed using the Annoy\nor HNSW libraries. Each search can be performed with a variety\nof different distance metrics, parallelization, and variable\nnumbers of neighbors. Range-based searches (to find all\nneighbors within a certain distance) are also supported.
